**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The ownership package sits at (indeed above) our preferred position:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (§ 14.1):** we own all Customer Data, Confidential Information and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for us. Reinforced by § 15.1 (no sale, no advertising use, no commingling, no model training without our written consent).
- **Deliverables (§ 14.2):** we own each Deliverable on creation, with a present-tense worldwide assignment from Vendor, equivalent personnel assignments, and further assurances.
- **Vendor IP with licence-back (§ 14.3 / § 13.2):** Vendor keeps only pre-existing Vendor Technology, and anything embedded in a Deliverable carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and have contractors support it, extending to Affiliates. Vendor must also flag material Vendor Technology pre-delivery and cannot slip in restrictive third-party material.
- **No joint ownership (§ 14.4):** expressly negated absent a separate signed instrument; feedback is voluntary and we retain unrestricted use of our own feedback.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: Deliverable ownership is conditioned on payment of Fees and on Order Form identification, and the Customer Data definition carves out anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to us or an individual. Neither assigns our IP or data to Copperleaf, so both fall within acceptable sub-element territory rather than a material failure.
